books.title: Mathematics
books.edition: Reprint 2026-27 (First Edition December 2006; Revised Edition October 2022; reprinted December 2025)

source.method: chapter titles and section headings from the book's Contents page, checked against each chapter PDF (Introduction and Summary sections are not topics; sections 6.4 and 13.2 are split by the criteria/methods they name, keeping the section heading in the topic title)

topics.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic
objectives: Student can express a composite number as a product of primes using a factor tree
Student can state the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic and explain that the prime factorisation is unique apart from order
Student can find the HCF and LCM of numbers by prime factorisation and use HCF x LCM = product of two numbers
Student can decide whether a number such as 4^n can end with the digit zero
visualIdeas: a factor tree breaking a number into primes
two numbers' prime factors shown in overlapping circles for HCF and LCM

topics.title: Revisiting Irrational Numbers
objectives: Student can use the theorem that if a prime p divides a^2 then p divides a
Student can prove that root 2, root 3 and similar numbers are irrational by contradiction
Student can show that sums and products involving an irrational number, such as 5 - root 3, are irrational
visualIdeas: a proof by contradiction laid out step by step

topics.title: Geometrical Meaning of the Zeroes of a Polynomial
objectives: Student can explain that the zeroes of a polynomial are the x-coordinates where its graph meets the x-axis
Student can recognise that a linear polynomial has one zero and a quadratic polynomial has at most two zeroes from its parabola
Student can read the number of zeroes of a polynomial from a given graph
visualIdeas: parabolas opening upward and downward cutting the x-axis at two, one or no points
a cubic curve meeting the x-axis three times

topics.title: Relationship between Zeroes and Coefficients of a Polynomial
objectives: Student can find the zeroes of a quadratic polynomial by factorisation and verify the relationships with its coefficients
Student can use sum of zeroes = -b/a and product of zeroes = c/a
Student can form a quadratic polynomial when the sum and product of its zeroes are given
visualIdeas: a table of polynomial, zeroes, sum and product

chapters.title: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables

topics.title: Graphical Method of Solution of a Pair of Linear Equations
objectives: Student can represent a pair of linear equations graphically as two lines
Student can identify intersecting, coincident and parallel lines and relate them to a unique solution, infinitely many solutions and no solution
Student can use the ratios a1/a2, b1/b2 and c1/c2 to decide whether a pair is consistent or inconsistent
visualIdeas: two lines intersecting, overlapping and running parallel on graph paper
a ratio table linked to each line picture

topics.title: Substitution Method
objectives: Student can solve a pair of linear equations by expressing one variable in terms of the other and substituting
Student can recognise from the result when a pair has no solution or infinitely many solutions
Student can form and solve a pair of equations from a word problem
visualIdeas: the substitution steps shown as a flow

topics.title: Elimination Method
objectives: Student can make the coefficients of one variable equal and eliminate it by adding or subtracting
Student can solve word problems such as the ratio of incomes and savings by elimination
Student can interpret a false statement or an identity obtained during elimination
visualIdeas: two equations aligned with matching coefficients cancelling

topics.title: Quadratic Equations
objectives: Student can identify a quadratic equation as ax^2 + bx + c = 0 with a not equal to 0
Student can represent word situations, such as the marbles of John and Jivanti or the toys made by a cottage industry, as quadratic equations
Student can check whether a given equation is quadratic after simplifying it
visualIdeas: a rectangle with sides x and 2x + 1 and its area

topics.title: Solution of a Quadratic Equation by Factorisation
objectives: Student can define a root of a quadratic equation and check a root by substitution
Student can find the roots of a quadratic equation by splitting the middle term and factorising
Student can solve a word problem by forming and factorising a quadratic equation
visualIdeas: the middle term split into two parts and factors grouped

topics.title: Nature of Roots
objectives: Student can use the quadratic formula and the discriminant b^2 - 4ac
Student can decide whether roots are two distinct real, two equal real or not real from the discriminant
Student can use the discriminant to answer questions such as whether a pole can be erected at a given point
visualIdeas: a parabola crossing, touching or missing the x-axis matched to discriminant signs

topics.title: Arithmetic Progressions
objectives: Student can define an arithmetic progression, its first term and its common difference
Student can decide whether a given list of numbers is an AP and write an AP from its first term and common difference
Student can distinguish finite and infinite APs
visualIdeas: equally spaced steps on a staircase
number lists with the difference between terms highlighted

topics.title: nth Term of an AP
objectives: Student can use a_n = a + (n - 1)d to find any term of an AP
Student can find the number of terms in a finite AP and decide whether a given number is a term
Student can solve word problems such as yearly salary increments using the nth term
visualIdeas: terms placed on a number line with jumps of d

topics.title: Sum of First n Terms of an AP
objectives: Student can derive S = n/2[2a + (n - 1)d] by writing the sum forwards and backwards
Student can use S = n/2(a + l) when the last term is known
Student can solve word problems such as total savings or prizes using the sum formula
visualIdeas: the sum written forwards and backwards with pairs adding to the same total

topics.title: Similar Figures
objectives: Student can distinguish similar figures from congruent figures
Student can state the conditions for two polygons with the same number of sides to be similar
Student can explain why all circles, all squares and all equilateral triangles are similar
visualIdeas: a photo and its enlargement side by side
a square and a rhombus with equal sides but different angles

topics.title: Similarity of Triangles
objectives: Student can state the conditions for two triangles to be similar
Student can prove and apply the Basic Proportionality Theorem (Theorem 6.1)
Student can apply its converse (Theorem 6.2) to show that a line is parallel to a side
visualIdeas: a triangle cut by a line parallel to its base with ratios marked

topics.title: Criteria for Similarity of Triangles: AAA and AA
objectives: Student can state the AAA similarity criterion (Theorem 6.3)
Student can explain why two pairs of equal angles (AA) are enough for similarity
Student can use AA similarity in problems such as the shadow of a girl under a lamp-post
visualIdeas: two triangles with matching angles coloured the same

topics.title: Criteria for Similarity of Triangles: SSS and SAS
objectives: Student can state the SSS similarity criterion (Theorem 6.4)
Student can state the SAS similarity criterion (Theorem 6.5)
Student can choose the right criterion to prove two triangles similar
visualIdeas: two triangles with proportional sides labelled

topics.title: Distance Formula
objectives: Student can derive the distance formula using Pythagoras theorem
Student can find the distance between two points and from a point to the origin
Student can use distances to decide whether points are collinear or form a particular figure
visualIdeas: two points on a grid joined by a right triangle

topics.title: Section Formula
objectives: Student can derive the section formula for a point dividing a segment internally in the ratio m1 : m2
Student can find the midpoint of a segment
Student can find the ratio in which a point divides a segment and the points of trisection
visualIdeas: a segment divided at P in ratio m1:m2 on a grid

topics.title: Trigonometric Ratios
objectives: Student can define sin, cos, tan, cosec, sec and cot of an acute angle in a right triangle
Student can explain why the ratios depend only on the angle
Student can find all trigonometric ratios when one ratio is given
visualIdeas: a right triangle with opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse labelled

topics.title: Trigonometric Ratios of Some Specific Angles
objectives: Student can find the trigonometric ratios of 45, 30 and 60 degrees using geometry
Student can state the ratios of 0 and 90 degrees
Student can use the table of values to evaluate expressions and find angles
visualIdeas: an equilateral triangle bisected to show 30 and 60 degrees
the standard values table

topics.title: Trigonometric Identities
objectives: Student can prove sin^2 A + cos^2 A = 1 and the two related identities
Student can express ratios in terms of each other using identities
Student can prove trigonometric identities
visualIdeas: a unit right triangle showing the Pythagoras link

topics.title: Heights and Distances
objectives: Student can define line of sight, angle of elevation and angle of depression
Student can draw a diagram for a heights-and-distances problem
Student can find heights and distances such as a tower or a building using trigonometric ratios
visualIdeas: an observer looking up at a tower with the angle of elevation marked
a person on a balcony looking down with the angle of depression

topics.title: Tangent to a Circle
objectives: Student can define a tangent as a line meeting a circle at exactly one point
Student can prove that the tangent at any point is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact
visualIdeas: a line rotating about a point until it touches the circle

topics.title: Number of Tangents from a Point on a Circle
objectives: Student can state the number of tangents from a point inside, on and outside a circle
Student can prove that tangents from an external point are equal in length
Student can use these results to solve problems
visualIdeas: two tangents from an external point with equal lengths marked

topics.title: Areas of Sector and Segment of a Circle
objectives: Student can identify minor and major sectors and segments of a circle
Student can find the area of a sector and the length of an arc using the angle of the sector
Student can find the area of a segment by subtracting the triangle's area from the sector's area
visualIdeas: a circle with a sector and segment shaded

topics.title: Surface Area of a Combination of Solids
objectives: Student can identify the basic solids that make up a combined solid
Student can find the total surface area of a combination of solids by adding only the visible curved surfaces
visualIdeas: a toy made of a cone on a hemisphere

topics.title: Volume of a Combination of Solids
objectives: Student can find the volume of a combination of solids by adding the volumes of its parts
Student can explain why volumes are simply added while surface areas are not
Student can solve problems such as the volume of air in a shed shaped as a cuboid with a half cylinder on top
visualIdeas: a shed made of a cuboid with a half cylinder on top

topics.title: Mean of Grouped Data: Direct Method
objectives: Student can find class marks as midpoints of class intervals
Student can find the mean of grouped data by the direct method
visualIdeas: a frequency table with a class-mark column

topics.title: Mean of Grouped Data: Assumed Mean Method
objectives: Student can choose an assumed mean and find deviations
Student can find the mean by the assumed mean method
visualIdeas: a table with a deviations column

topics.title: Mean of Grouped Data: Step-deviation Method
objectives: Student can find the mean by the step-deviation method
Student can choose an appropriate method for given data
visualIdeas: a table with step-deviation values

topics.title: Mode of Grouped Data
objectives: Student can identify the modal class
Student can find the mode using the formula
visualIdeas: a histogram with the modal class highlighted

topics.title: Median of Grouped Data
objectives: Student can make a cumulative frequency table
Student can make less than and more than cumulative frequency distributions
Student can find the median class and use the median formula for grouped data
visualIdeas: a cumulative frequency table

topics.title: Probability - A Theoretical Approach
objectives: Student can define theoretical probability as favourable outcomes over all outcomes
Student can identify elementary events, sure events and impossible events
Student can use P(E) + P(not E) = 1
Student can find probabilities in problems with coins, dice and cards
visualIdeas: a die with outcomes listed
a deck of cards sorted by suits
